counterexample: git reset --hard in a shell call with no user request: before PV2-01 the hook allowed it silently; now it asks with the authority rule, and the clause still forbids running it without an explicit request.
note: The PreToolUse hook now asks before repository-changing Git with the K0 table; read-only Git runs; an existing deny wins; git-workflow names the hook and says the prompt is not authorization. GOV-015 (do not run repository-changing Git unless explicitly requested) is carried by the CLAUDE.md authority clause in all six; the ask adds a confirmation point, not a permission.
quotes: asks the user to confirm Git commands it classifies as repository-changing
